severity: ROOT CAUSE of the visible hand shaking -- and a candidate cause of the noise floor
claim: RL fine-tuning induced a ~1.7 Hz open-close oscillation of the fingers that neither the demonstrations nor the SFT policy contain. The visible 'hand shaking' is not jitter, noise, or chunk-boundary jerk: it is the RL policy's predicted finger trajectory pumping ~0.6 rad every 30-step chunk.

measurement.protocol: same probe, same frozen condition 21, deterministic, full 690-step episode; finger joint 47 (1:1 with the policy's raw finger command via coupling=1.0)
measurement.spectral: 92% of the RLPD finger-command energy sits below 2 Hz with the pump at ~1.7 Hz (once per 0.6 s chunk); sign-flip rate 0.12, i.e. smooth large swings, not high-frequency noise
measurement.demonstration_behaviour: finger at 0.00 through the reach, closes 0 -> 1.30 rad over ~1 s, then holds rock-steady for the remainder of the episode
measurement.demo_bandwidth: 97.6% of demonstrated hand-signal energy below 1.0 Hz

attribution: SFT swing 0.065 vs RLPD 0.580 under identical execution: the oscillation is CREATED by RL fine-tuning, not inherited. Mechanism consistent with the literature (CAPS, Mysore et al., ICRA 2021, arXiv:2012.06644): exploration noise (std 0.2) on the hand dims enters the replay buffer, the reward contains no action-smoothness term, and the actor update fits the roughness.

why_earlier_fixes_failed.chunk_blending: fixed the boundary discontinuity (0.90 -> 0.15 rad) but the pump lives INSIDE the chunk; A/B correctly showed no effect
why_earlier_fixes_failed.why_it_looked_like_jitter: the retargeter drives proximal+intermediate from one command (coupling 1.0), doubling the visual amplitude on the fingers

connections: Candidate cause of the post-grasp nondeterminism noise floor: a hand pumping 0.58 rad/chunk around a 20 mm barrel makes contact outcomes chaotic (carry Jaccard 0.066 across identical runs) while the pre-contact stage stays reproducible (grasp Jaccard 0.99).
Candidate cause of grasp-never-becomes-transport: the object is squeezed and released repeatedly mid-hold.
The SFT stochastic successes are consistent: a smooth hand plus sampled arm variation.

fixes.execution_layer_now: rlinf/envs/isaaclab/tasks/g1_piston_action_filter.py -- demonstration-envelope filter: causal 2nd-order low-pass at f_c=1.2 Hz + slew cap 0.175/step, every constant measured from the 11 demos (cutoff chosen as the highest halving the measured pump while tracking demos to <0.05 RMSE and closing a grasp to 90% in 0.52 s). Carries state across chunks, so it subsumes blending. 11 unit tests, incl. halving the swing on the real recorded commands.
fixes.training_time_future: CAPS-style temporal smoothness penalty on consecutive actions in the SAC/RLPD actor loss; removes the pathology at the source but needs retraining (~11 h/arm).

dose_response.observation: SAC (no demonstration replay) oscillates 1.594 rad/chunk -- nearly the full finger range (limit 1.7) -- while RLPD (50% demonstration transitions per batch) oscillates 0.580, about 3x less, under identical execution and reward.
dose_response.interpretation: Demonstration replay partially protects action smoothness during RL fine-tuning. With no smoothness term in the reward and Gaussian exploration noise entering the replay, the demo fraction is the only thing anchoring the actor to demonstration-like action dynamics.
dose_response.caveat: n=1 checkpoint per algorithm at different training budgets (415k vs 690k); a training-time confound (budget) is not excluded. The earlier per-checkpoint probes suggest the oscillation grows with training in both algorithms.

validation_results.protocol: Pre-registered before data: grasp below the baseline worst (0.96) = real regression; carry only counts outside the 8-run noise range [0.00, 0.36]; SFT stochastic success (0.16 in two independent draws) must survive.

full_dim_filter_rlpd_415k_det_n25.verdict: REGRESSION. Grasp 0.68 is below every one of the 8 baseline runs (worst 0.96). The ~0.3 s filter lag on the ARM dims plausibly breaks reach/grasp timing. Carry 0.00 is inside the baseline noise range -- no resolvable effect.

full_dim_filter_sft_stochastic_n25.baseline: 0.16 success in each of two independent unfiltered draws (disjoint condition sets)
full_dim_filter_sft_stochastic_n25.verdict: The filter DESTROYS the SFT stochastic successes (0/25) and even eliminates reaching. Mechanistic implication: the SFT successes are driven by high-frequency components of the sampled actions -- the behaviour that completes the task lives ABOVE the demonstrated bandwidth. Do not use the full-dim filter for stochastic execution.

hand_only_filter_rlpd_415k_det_n25.verdict: PASS. Grasp 1.00 vs baseline range [0.96, 1.00]: filtering only the 12 hand dims (14-25, arm bit-exact) fully restores grasp. This confirms the full-dim regression was arm reach-phase lag, not the hand smoothing. Carry 0.04 is inside the 8-run noise range [0.00, 0.36] -- the filter neither helps nor hurts post-grasp outcomes resolvably. Hand-only is the deliverable execution-layer fix: task-neutral, removes the visible oscillation.

in_sim_smoothness_probe_full_dim.file: handdyn_rlpd_filt2.json + handdyn_rlpd_filt2_cmd.npy (cond 21, RLPD@415k, det, filter 1.2 Hz all dims)
in_sim_smoothness_probe_full_dim.note: The filter works as designed mechanically (halves the pump, subsumes blending); its failures are task-level, not implementation-level.

hand_filter_plus_blend6_rlpd_415k_det_n2.verdict: PASS (pre-registered gate grasp >= 0.92). The combination of the hand-only demo-envelope filter (1.2 Hz) and 6-step arm chunk blending is task-neutral: grasp 0.96 inside the baseline range [0.96, 1.00], carry 0.12 inside noise. This is the PRESENTATION execution config: hands smoothed, arm boundary snap (up to 1 rad) ramped out.

hand_filter_fc06_plus_blend6_rlpd_415k_d.verdict: PASS (pre-registered gate grasp >= 0.92). fc=0.6 Hz on the hand dims plus 6-step arm blending keeps grasp at 1.00 -- the grasp is robust to slow finger closure. This is the calmest validated execution config; the remaining visible motion is the sub-1 Hz ARM sway, which only the training-time fix can address.

conclusion: Execution-layer fix validated: DemoEnvelopeFilter (f_c=1.2 Hz, slew 0.175/step) applied to the 12 hand dims only. Grasp preserved at 1.00 (n=25 det, frozen suite), carry inside noise, boundary jumps 0.90 -> 0.01 rad, per-step hand motion ~3x smoother. Full-dim filtering is REJECTED (arm lag breaks grasp: 0.68). Stochastic-SFT filtering is REJECTED (destroys the 0.16 success rate; those successes ride on high-frequency sampled noise). Training-time counterpart for future runs: SMOOTH_LAMBDA (CAPS L_T) in train_sac.py, default 0.

in_band_residual.finding: RL fine-tuning also induced SLOW (sub-1 Hz) oscillation, on the ARM as well as the fingers. Sub-1 Hz command sway, same condition: joint 12 SFT 0.43 -> RLPD 0.83 rad; joint 16 0.14 -> 0.60; joint 22 0.15 -> 0.66; joint 26 0.40 -> 1.03; joint 28 0.16 -> 0.71. SAC seed 2 is equal or worse (j16 1.66). The hand filter + blend leave it unchanged (in-band, arm unfiltered): visible residual motion in the filtered videos is this sway plus a 0.8 Hz +-0.17 rad finger flex.
in_band_residual.implication: Execution-layer filtering is structurally unable to remove it: it lives at 0.2-0.8 Hz where demonstrated reaching also lives, and the pre-registered full-dim A/B already showed arm filtering breaks grasp. The complete fix is training-time: CAPS smoothness penalty (SMOOTH_LAMBDA) or heavier demonstration replay (dose-response: RLPD 50% replay has ~3x less oscillation than SAC).
in_band_residual.files: handdyn_sft_cmd.npy vs blendcmd_b0_cmd.npy vs handdyn_rlpd_handblend_cmd.npy vs handdyn_sac2_cmd.npy

training_time_fix_experiment.design: Continue RLPD from rlpd_ckpt_step415140.pt (WARM_CKPT) with SMOOTH_LAMBDA=100 (CAPS L_T on the deterministic squashed chunk, active dims), wall-clock bounded at 2.5 h, MAX_ENV_STEPS=120000, checkpoints every 15000 env steps. All other hyperparameters identical to the original RLPD run (demo_frac 0.5, UTD 0.5, batch 8, seed 0).

gates.PASS: deterministic-chunk smoothness penalty drops >= 50% from its warm-start value AND final-checkpoint grasp on the frozen suite >= 0.92 (n=25 det)
gates.FAIL_behaviour: grasp < 0.92 -- the penalty broke the behaviour
gates.FAIL_ineffective: penalty does not move -- the fix does not work at this scale/duration

training_time_fix_experiment.rationale: lambda=100 makes the measured pathology cost ~0.1-0.3 against actor-loss terms ~3 while demo-like motion costs ~1e-4. L_T mainly targets the fast pump; the sub-1 Hz sway has small per-step diffs and may move less -- report both.

lambda0_control.penalty_metric: 1.88e-3 -> 3.37e-3 (+79%: continued RL further DEGRADES smoothness by default)

verdicts.pre_registered_gate: MISS by 3 points on the letter (-47% vs the required -50% against the static warm-start value); grasp gate PASSED (1.00).
verdicts.controlled_comparison: The penalty is causally responsible for the smoothing: against the lambda=0 counterfactual (3.37e-3) the lambda=100 policy is 3.4x smoother, and arm sway only moves under the penalty. Task metrics are statistically indistinguishable between the two continuations (lift 0.72 vs 0.68, return 8.56 vs 7.71) -- the smoothness penalty cost nothing.
verdicts.task_note: Both continuations exceed the ENTIRE 8-run baseline range on lift, tube and return (baseline lift <= 0.56, tube <= 0.24, return <= 6.07). Attribution: the additional training, not the penalty. Single evaluation each -- interpret via the noise-floor caveat, though exceeding the full observed range on three metrics simultaneously in both arms is unlikely to be noise.

training_time_fix_experiment.render_termination_note: The first smoothed renders ended at chunk 3: the underlying IsaacLab task has a single termination term (misleadingly named "success") that resets when the object leaves x(-0.42,1.0), y(0.2,0.7), or z<0.5. The smoothed policy transports the piston ~0.17 m toward the y=0.2 boundary; whether it crosses mid-episode varies by draw (contact nondeterminism -- same checkpoint, same condition: one render terminated at chunk 3, the diagnostic re-render ran all 23 chunks with te/tr false at every one of 1380 logged steps, final root y=0.2345). Implication for the continuation evals: episodes that cross the boundary truncate early, which biases lift/return DOWN, so lift 0.72 / 0.68 are conservative. mean_return comparisons across arms with different truncation rates carry that caveat. The full-length render (diag_smooth_*, step_log included) replaced the truncated draw in the comparison video; the truncated draw is retained as evidence.
